chunks: Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from the one who informed him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
‘Whoever performs Tawaf (circumambulation) between these two stones, Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, is released from Ihram, except for the one who is ushering the sacrificial animal (Qarin/Mufrid with Hady).’

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Released from Ihram / Permitted to end restrictions
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa (the second of the two hills)
key_terms.سَائِقَ الْهَدْيِ: The one ushering/bringing the sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim's Ihram end after performing Tawaf between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa is the final act that terminates the state of Ihram for most pilgrims, distinguishing the ruling for those performing Tamattu' or Qiran who must offer a sacrifice. It highlights the specific exception of the 'Saiq al-Hady' (one who brings the sacrificial animal), whose Ihram remains binding until the actual slaughter, underscoring the link between ritual movement and sacrificial obligation. This ruling is foundational in determining when prohibited acts of Ihram become permissible again during the Hajj rites.
